configuration.change: Sharp full-field DeMCELS H-alpha filaments and diffuse gas, with SHASSA at coverage gaps.

overlapCalibration.method: Robust additive differences at matching sky coordinates in overlapping DeMCELS tiles. A weighted graph solution fixes relative zeros. Each connected survey component then gets one additive absolute zero from SHASSA low-emission (<40 R) samples. Native gains, line ratios and filament structure are unchanged. No Horálek pixels.

source.coverageRule: The union no-data boundary is distance-tapered over60 arcseconds after stitching. Interior coverage is exactly one, independent of splat density or overlap count.
source.method: Native 0.27 arcsecond DN are area-averaged in 11x11 blocks (2.97 arcseconds), converted with the published DR1 flux scale, then bilinearly deposited on a 3 arcsecond TAN grid. Overlapping tiles are edge-weighted; any uncovered output pixels remain absent and use SHASSA in the field loader. Relative additive sky offsets come only from matching DeMCELS overlap pixels. Each connected component has one SHASSA absolute-zero anchor. Native gains and local filament contrast stay fixed; this is survey calibration, not an appearance fit. The overlap graph and residuals are recorded.
source.calibration: Points et al. 2024 DR1: 2.4e-18 erg/s/cm2 per released DN, divided by native pixel solid angle and 5.661e-18 per Rayleigh per square arcsecond. No exposure-time division. N662 includes [NII]; no unmeasured spatial [NII] correction is claimed.
source.limitations: DR1 covers 54 square degrees, not every point in the 10-degree field. Tile and chip gaps use the low-resolution fallback. Continuum subtraction can retain stellar residuals. Native 1.3 arcsecond seeing is reduced to 3 arcsecond sampling; the physical model and 512-pixel display are coarser.

quality.source: DeMCELS DR1 checked against independently calibrated SHASSA Field013.
quality.tolerance: Adopted data-quality bound: the larger of 5 R and 50% of the reference surface brightness. Full confidence below that disagreement; a smooth transition to zero at twice the bound. These are source-quality tolerances, not parameters fitted to Horálek.
quality.method: Both line surveys are compared over exactly the same covered sky cells after a 5 arcminute box mean. Inconsistent DeMCELS background is excluded from the sharp-data weight, leaving the measured SHASSA fill. This does not claim to recover the missing exposure masks or remove every stellar continuum residual.
quality.limitations: A valid sharp feature may lose confidence if the broad-bandpasses or local background disagree. The fallback is coarse. This conservative selection cannot turn incomplete data into complete 3 arcsecond coverage.

source.source: DeMCELS DR1 continuum-subtracted full-field mosaic; SHASSA outside coverage.
source.unsupportedRule: Cells outside both observed footprints remain unmodelled, with a false source mask; they are not measured zero emission. The adopted physical support fade is unchanged.
source.diffuseMethod: A broad 200 pc half-width mean supplies DIG morphology. A single coefficient partitions 35% of integrated line emission into DIG, following the 30–40% Kennicutt et al. 1995 range. Unassigned catalogue emission is recorded separately.
source.transport: Every 3 arcsecond sky-pixel centre inside each projected physical-cell quadrilateral is area-averaged, with coverage weights. Signed emission is averaged before the positive-emission clamp. The measured warp supplies projected sky area; multiplication by squared heliocentric distance converts solid angle to projected physical area before the field is lifted. The global normalization removes the constant angular unit.
source.dustCorrection: The same OGLE foreground internal A_V correction and adopted 5.5–6.5 kpc support fade as l34. No Horálek spatial pixels.
source.fallback: SHASSA Field013 supplies gaps, with the 60 arcsecond native-tile edge taper. The same SHASSA exterior sky zero is subtracted from both sources before blending. No-data is never interpreted as zero emission.
source.depth: Each cloud is a finite isotropic kernel. Its center receives a deterministic line-of-sight depth whose FWHM is its parent nebula geometric-mean sky diameter; width is resolution-limited. In l35, cloud luminosity includes its squared observer-distance ratio after the depth draw, preserving the observed relative sky flux before owner normalization. Published 30 Dor shell chords are used where intersected. The surrounding diffuse gas stays on the 150 pc Gaussian warped layer. No columns are extruded along the Earth direction.
source.relativeLight: The full survey supplies each catalogue region’s relative on-sky shape. Each region is normalized to its accepted parent luminosity; those amplitudes stay fixed. Regions unresolved or absent in the coarse fallback keep their prior geometry. The diffuse map has unit area, with its global luminosity set by the recorded budget and DIG fraction before the common gas RGB grade. In l35 the previous compact plus analytic budget is redistributed, not increased. Its DIG luminosity is the adopted35% Kennicutt prior. The separately recorded shape fraction reflects catalogue footprint assignment, not an independent DIG luminosity measurement.

details.frozen: All stars, grades except gas, bar, warp, dust and adopted stellar/diffuse layer heights.
